test.title: Nuclear Physics - Test 1
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text:
From the statements given below :

(A) The angular momentum of an electron in nth orbit is an integral multiple of h.

(B) Nuclear forces do not obey inverse square law.

(C) Nuclear forces are spin dependent.

(D) Nuclear forces are central and charge independent.

(E) Stability of nucleus is inversely proportional to the value of packing fraction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

For a nucleus XZA having mass number A and atomic number Z

A. The surface energy per nucleon (bs)=–a1A23.

B. The Coulomb contribution to the binding energy bc=−a2Z(Z−1)A43.

C. The volume energy bv = a3A

D. Decrease in the binding energy is proportional to surface area.

E. While estimating the surface energy, it is assumed that each nucleon interacts with 12 nucleons. (a1, a2 and a3 are constants)

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}\hline & \text{LIST-I} & & \text{LIST-II} \\ \hline \text{A.} & \begin{array}{l} { }_0^1 \mathrm{n}+{ }_{92}^{235} \mathrm{U} \\ \rightarrow{ }_{54}^{140} \mathrm{Xe}+{ }_{38}^{94} \mathrm{Sr}+2{ }_0^1 \mathrm{n} \end{array} & \text{I.} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Chemical} \\ \text{reaction} \end{array} \\ \hline \text{B.} & 2 \mathrm{H}_2+\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} & \text{II.} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Fusion} \\ \text{with +ve} \\ \text{Q value} \end{array} \\ \hline \text{C.} & { }_1^2 \mathrm{H}+{ }_1^2 \mathrm{H} \rightarrow{ }_2^3 \mathrm{He}+{ }_0^1 \mathrm{n} & \text{III.} & \text{Fission} \\ \hline \text{D.} & { }_1^1 \mathrm{H}+{ }_1^3 \mathrm{H} \rightarrow{ }_1^2 \mathrm{H}+{ }_1^2 \mathrm{H} & \text{IV.} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Fusion} \\ \text{with -ve Q} \\ \text{value} \end{array} \\ \hline\end{array}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

Which of the following figure represents the variation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ln</mi><mfenced><mfrac><mi>R</mi><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac></mfenced></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ln</mi><mi>A</mi></math> (if <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo></math> radius of a nucleus and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo></math> its mass number)

Consider the following statements:
A. Atoms of each element emit characteristics spectrum.
B. According to Bohr's Postulate, an electron in a hydrogen atom revolves in a certain stationary orbit.

C. The density of nuclear matter depends on the size of the nucleus.
D. A free neutron is stable but a free proton decay is possible.
E. Radioactivity is an indication of the instability of nuclei. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

Consider the nuclear fission, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Ne</mi><mn>20</mn></msup><mo>→</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>He</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>12</mn></msup></math>. Given that the binding energy/nucleon of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Ne</mi><mn>20</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi>He</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mtext> </mtext></math>and<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext> </mtext><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>12</mn></msup></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8.03</mn><mtext> </mtext><mi>MeV</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>7.86</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math>, respectively. Identify the correct statement:

options.text: Energy of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>72</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math> has to be supplied.

Which of the following process is allowed by momentum and energy conservation :

options.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mo>→</mo></math> deuterium atom (electron bound to the nucleus)

question.text: A nucleus with mass number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>184</mn></math> initially at rest emits an <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>-</mo></math>particle. If the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> value of the reaction is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi><mo>,</mo></math> calculate the kinetic energy of the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>-</mo></math> particle.

Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : The nuclear density of nuclides B510, L36i, F2656e, N1020e and B83209i can be arranged as ρBiN>ρFeN>ρNeN>ρBN>ρLiN

Reason R : The radius R of nucleus is related to its mass number A as R=R0 A13, where R0 is a constant.

In the light of the above statement, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

question.text:
The energy released in the fusion of $2 \mathrm{~kg}$ of hydrogen deep in the sun is $E_H$ and the energy released in the fission of $2 \mathrm{~kg}$ of ${ }^{235} \mathrm{U}$ is $E_U$. The ratio $\frac{E_H}{E_U}$ is approximately:
(Consider the fusion reaction as $4 \mid H+2 \mathrm{e}^{-} \rightarrow{ }_2^4 \mathrm{He}+2 v+6 \gamma+26.7 \mathrm{MeV}$, energy released in the fission reaction of ${ }^{235} \mathrm{U}$ is $200 \mathrm{MeV}$ per fission nucleus and $\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}=$ $\left.6.023 \times 10^{23}\right)$
A nucleus at rest disintegrates into two smaller nuclei with their masses in the ratio of $2: 1$. After disintegration they will move :

options.text: in the same direction with same speed.
in opposite directions with the same speed.
in opposite directions with speed in the ratio of $2: 1$ respectively.
in opposite directions with speed in the ratio of $1: 2$ respectively.

question.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The density of the copper $\left({ }_{29}^{64} \mathrm{Cu}\right)$ nucleus is greater than that of the carbon $\left({ }_6^{12} \mathrm{C}\right)$ nucleus.
Reason (R): The nucleus of mass number A has a radius proportional to $\mathrm{A}^{1 / 3}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: $(\mathrm{A})$ is correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not correct
$(\mathrm{A})$ is not correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is correct
Both $(\mathrm{A})$ and $(\mathrm{R})$ are correct and $(\mathrm{R})$ is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

options.text: not possible as proton mass is less than the neutron mass
not possible but neutron to proton conversion is possible
always possible as it is associated only with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></math> decay

Assertion (A) : The binding energy per nucleon is found to be practically independent of the atomic number A, for nuclei with mass numbers between 30 and 170.
Reason (R): Nuclear force is long range.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

question.text:
